newsitem.title: GERMANY: Cheaper coal boosts VEW Energie earnings.
newsitem.headline: Cheaper coal boosts VEW Energie earnings.

text.p: German energy group VEW Energie said on Wednesday that savings from cheaper coal prices helped boost its pre-tax profits by 20.6 percent to 306 million marks.

The profit growth should continue for full-year 1996, even though sales in the period dropped 0.4 percent to 4.24 billion marks at the group, Egbert Pottgiesser, chief financial officer of VEW Energie said.
Pottgiesser said that savings from a lower payroll and increased contributions from the groups subsidiaries would combine with cheaper material costs to help boost the full-year earnings figure.
VEW Energie is the electricity and gas unit of the utility VEW AG and it was founded in 1995 in conjunction with the municipal power companies from the city of Dortmund.
From the year 2000 the group also hopes to report income from its east German subsidiaries.
However, management board chairman Hans-Diether Imhoff said there could be "serious disputes" in store with the development agency for the former East Germany, the BvS.
